$comment: Baseline-label filter contract, read by BOTH hdf-engine/go/filter_test.go and test/query.test.ts so the two implementations cannot drift. Decisions pinned here rather than in prose: (1) the predicate is BASELINE-level, checked once per baseline beside the existing name filter, because a label is a property of the baseline and not of any requirement in it — so a matching baseline contributes every requirement inside it. (2) The form mirrors tag's key:value string with a glob on the VALUE only; keys are open by schema (additionalProperties: {type: string}) so a key nothing carries selects nothing, and that is correct rather than an error. (3) A label value is exactly one string, so this does NOT reuse tagMatchesGlob, whose value may be a list. (4) An absent key matches nothing INCLUDING against '*': the predicate asks about a label the baseline does not carry, and there is nothing to match. (5) A colonless predicate names no key and can never match any document, so it is REFUSED at the CLI boundary (hdf query --baseline-label, and threshold rule validation) rather than allowed to select nothing — selecting nothing and being ignored produce the same forever-green gate under a max bound. The filter itself still selects nothing for one, which is the safe half of that pair, and that is pinned below.
fixtureNote: query-fixture.json's FIRST baseline carries labels {environment: production, component: rhel9-host, team: platform-sre}; its SECOND is deliberately unlabelled, which is what makes the exclusion cases meaningful. Unfiltered the fixture returns all 5 requirements.

cases.name: a different key on the same baseline
glob on the value, as tags allow
a key nothing carries matches nothing
a value nothing carries matches nothing
a glob cannot stand in for an absent key
a colonless predicate selects nothing rather than everything
